source.authors: Yang X, Ran H, Jiang Y, Lu Z, Wei G, Li J
source.title: Fine structure of the compound eyes of the crepuscular moth Grapholita molesta (Busck 1916) (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae)

method: facets counted on nail-polish cornea replicas of the removed eyes, photographed under a light microscope (Sections 2.4, 2.5)
conditions: adults of a laboratory strain derived from wild-caught larvae from a peach orchard in Shunping County, Hebei, China (Section 2.1), kept at 26 C, 15L:9D; eyes of 5 males and 5 females removed for facet counts (Section 2.4; Table 1 N = 5 per sex); males 1072 ± 37, females 1029 ± 15 (Table 1 does not state whether ± is SD or SE); Section 3.1 prints p = 0.077 for the sex difference (independent samples t-test, Section 2.5); the two sexes are filed as separate records; for its light-adaptation experiments the paper exposed specimens to one of four intensities (10000, 100, 1 or 0.01 mW/m2) for 2 h before decapitation at 20:00 (Section 2.1) and used five of each sex per intensity for TEM (Section 2.2); Section 2.4 does not say whether the facet-count moths were light-treated or from which group they came
note: new trait: ommatidia_count (key already in use on main). Table 1 row quoted without its merged 'Compound eyes' group cell; the fetch rendered the table as text, so spacing between cells is the fetch's. Family and order as printed in the title; name accepted in docs/views/gaps/gbif-names.tsv (GBIF backbone, ACCEPTED). Page prints no licence sentence; Crossref single-DOI lookup (filter=doi) gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Frontiers prints a volume and article number but no issue. Interommatidial angle for this species is already on main (sweep-56).

source.authors: Yang X, Ran H, Jiang Y, Lu Z, Wei G, Li J
source.title: Fine structure of the compound eyes of the crepuscular moth Grapholita molesta (Busck 1916) (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae)

method: facet diameter measured on SEM micrographs as the corner to corner distance of the hexagonal corneal surface (Section 2.5) (the text's gloss)
conditions: mean 15.2 ± 0.3 over 60 facets (Table 1; ± not stated as SD or SE); number of individuals and sex not stated for this row; laboratory strain derived from wild-caught larvae from a peach orchard in Shunping County, Hebei, China (collected August 2020); the light history of the SEM specimens is not stated (the four-intensity exposure is described for the light-adaptation experiments and TEM, Sections 2.1, 2.2); sexes pooled and no sex test for facet size reported; Section 3.2 gives the corneal lens diameter as 15.8 µm (the figure used for the 4.3° interommatidial angle, main sweep-56), which the paper does not reconcile with the 15.2 µm of Section 3.1 and Table 1
note: new trait: facet_diameter_um (key already in use on main). source.authors: Yang X, Ran H, Jiang Y, Lu Z, Wei G, Li J
source.title: Fine structure of the compound eyes of the crepuscular moth Grapholita molesta (Busck 1916) (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae)

conditions: mean 62.3 ± 2.2, N = 12 in Table 1 (the Methods do not say whether N counts ommatidia or individuals); 'about 62.3 um' as printed; total rhabdom length (the centrally-fused distal rhabdom rod is 31.4 µm long and 1.8 µm wide at its distal end); sex of the 12 not stated, but TEM used five of each sex at each of four light-adaptation states (10000, 100, 1 or 0.01 mW/m2, 2 h; Section 2.2), and the paper gives no per-sex or per-state rhabdom length; it reports no significant differences between the eyes of males and females (Section 3.2) and says the size of the rhabdom was not obviously different between light-adaptation states (Section 4.2, no test given), while the position of the distal rhabdom differed significantly between states, the retinula cells pulling away from the cone in bright light (Section 3.3); laboratory strain from wild-caught larvae, Shunping County, Hebei, China
quote: Each ommatidium contains eight retinula cells to form a rhabdom, measuring about 62.3 um in total length.
